title: gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/secret-scanning/alerts?state=${state}[&resolution=false_positive,wont_fix,used_in_tests]&sort=updated&direction=desc&per_page=100
description: The repository's secret scanning alerts, the open ones, and those resolved as a false positive, as won't fix, or as used in tests, which kit takes for dismissed, asked for in `modules/bash/forge/github.sh` (forge/github:secret-scanning-alerts, and forge/github:bypasses for the resolved) and folded in `modules/jq/forge.jq` (forge::github_secret_scanning, forge::github_dismissals). gh api --paginate --slurp prints one array of the pages, each an array of alerts. state takes one value, open or resolved, as GitHub answers 400 `State needs to be either 'open' or 'resolved'` otherwise, checked live. A repository with secret scanning off answers 404 `Secret scanning is disabled on this repository.`, checked live: the scanner is off. A classic token needs `repo` or `security_events`, and the caller must be an admin of the repository or its organization. The types are those of GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/secret-scanning/alerts in GitHub's REST OpenAPI, as https://docs.github.com/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning#list-secret-scanning-alerts-for-a-repository describes them: resolution is false_positive, wont_fix, revoked, used_in_tests, or null.
